subject: physical-education
title: Unit assessment: refining through self-review and adult feedback under transfer
focus: refining through self-review and adult feedback
essentialQuestion: How do I build a sequence that says something and still works as movement?
privacySafeScenario: Compose, refine, and document a structured movement sequence, then present it to one trusted adult or submit a complete written or notated description instead.
studentTask: Learner works refining through self-review and adult feedback in a longer sequence built across several sessions and refined from the learner’s own review rather than from instruction at a self-set intensity, then records what held, what degraded first, and how this occasion differed from the earlier one.
knowledgeCheck: In one concise response, say which feature of refining through self-review and adult feedback degraded first under the added demand, why, and what you would change before the next attempt.
completionCriteria: The learner holds refining through self-review and adult feedback in a longer sequence built across several sessions and refined from the learner’s own review rather than from instruction, in whatever version their body and setting allow.
The learner names what degraded first and why, rather than reporting only whether it worked.
The learner compares this occasion with the earlier one and says what actually changed.
adaptationChoices: Sequences may be seated, small-range, hand-and-arm only, or built at any tempo. Notation, storyboard, or written description is a full alternative to performing.
extensionChallenge: Design the next progression of refining through self-review and adult feedback yourself, or coach the transfer condition to someone else so that they succeed with it — without completing another learner's graded work.
accessibilitySupports: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, demonstrated, or described responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, rest-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, intensity, range, equipment, or response mode.
Every movement task has a seated, supported, reduced-range, reduced-pace, and solo version that reaches the same standard.
Sequences may be seated, small-range, hand-and-arm only, or built at any tempo. Notation, storyboard, or written description is a full alternative to performing.

optionalReflection.prompt: Invite the learner to notice where refining through self-review and adult feedback shows up outside the session under real conditions. No purchase, account creation, photograph, recording, or public performance is required.

neverRequires: This task never requires body weight, height, BMI, or body-fat percentage.
This task never requires calorie counting or a diet or weight-loss goal.
This task never requires disclosing private medical history, a diagnosis, or sexual history.
This task never requires a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as proof.
This task never requires a public performance or an audience.
